The company states 140,000+ bots and 500M messages (with measurement basis requiring clarification — see consistency note on [C3, S2] vs [C3, S3]) in a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2], and 500M messages/month elsewhere [S3], indicating platform-level usage, but how ManyChat monetises that usage is not found in the extracted evidence. The sector is profiled as Software [P2] and the stage as Series A [P1], but neither informs the revenue mechanism. Information Readiness Score: 10/100 Present: • Traction metrics: the company states 140,000+ bots and 500M messages (slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16') [S1, S2] • A messages/month figure of 500M stated separately [S3] • Funding raised figure narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt: $23.1M [C1, S4] • Stage profile: Series A [P1] • Sector profile: Software [P2] Needs Validation: • Whether 500M messages is a cumulative total or a monthly figure — the two slides present conflicting bases [C3, C2] • The $23.1M raised figure (per Pitch Deck Hunt) — undated and not independently verified [C1] • All traction figures — none independently verified [C2, C3, C4, S1, S2, S3] Next evidence to supply: Audited or reviewed financial statements including revenue, gross margin, and a dated cash balance, plus a clarification of whether the 500M messages figure is cumulative or a monthly run rate. Supported Points • Pitch Deck Hunt lists $23.1M raised [C1, S4]; this is narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt and undated, and was not independently verified, so it cannot be treated as a confirmed funding total but is on record as a stated figure. • The company states 140,000+ bots and 500M messages in a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2], indicating claimed platform scale at that point in time, though neither figure has been independently verified. Open Concerns • The messaging volume metric is internally inconsistent: the slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' states '500M messages' without an interval [C3, S2], while a separate page states '500M messages/month' [C3, S3]. Whether the figure is cumulative or a monthly run rate is unresolved and directly affects the interpretation of growth trajectory. • No revenue, burn, or unit-economics data is present in the extracted evidence, leaving the commercial viability of the stated user and message volumes entirely unassessable. • The $23.1M raised figure [C1, S4] is narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt, is undated, and was not independently verified — it is unknown when this capital was raised, in how many tranches, or what remains. • The complete absence of team, product, problem, and market information in the extracted evidence means that core diligence inputs — defensibility, founder quality, and market sizing — cannot be evaluated from this material. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece of evidence is an audited or reviewed income statement with dated revenue figures and gross margin, which would establish whether the stated message and bot volume translates to a scalable commercial business. Without it, the traction metrics [S1, S2, S3] remain unanchored to any financial outcome.
